Question.
Let kk be a local non-Archimedean field with integers OkO_{k}, uniformizer tt, and residue field 𝔽q\mathbb{F}_{q} of characteristic pp. Let k˘\breve{k} be the completion of the maximal unramified extension of kk, and let Ok˘O_{\breve{k}} be its integers. Consider an unramified reductive group GG over kk. Suppose TT is an unramified torus of GG and let UU be the unipotent radical of a Borel subgroup containing TT and defined over k˘\breve{k}.

Fix a parahoric model 𝒢\mathcal{G} of GG over the integers OkO_{k}. Fix an integer r≥1r\geq 1. We may consider Gr:=𝒢⁡(Ok˘/tr​Ok˘)G_{r}:=\mathcal{G}(O_{\breve{k}}/t^{r}O_{\breve{k}}) as a perfect algebraic group (of perfectly finite type) over the residue field 𝔽q\mathbb{F}_{q} by using the positive loop functor (also called jet scheme) construction. The Frobenius FF of k˘/k\breve{k}/k acts naturally on GrG_{r}. Also, the closures of T,UT,U in 𝒢\mathcal{G} define by the same procedure subgroups Tr,UrT_{r},U_{r} of GrG_{r} (with TrT_{r} being FF-stable but UrU_{r} not). Let

It admits an action of (Gr)F×(Tr)F(G_{r})^{F}\times(T_{r})^{F} by (g,t):x↦g​x​t(g,t):x\mapsto gxt. For a character ϕ\phi of (Tr)F(T_{r})^{F}, let RT,U,r​(ϕ)R_{T,U,r}(\phi) denote the alternating sum of the ϕ\phi-isotypic parts of the ℓ\ell-adic étale cohomology groups of XrX_{r}, regarded as a virtual (Gr)F(G_{r})^{F}-module (very similar to classical Deligne–Lusztig theory).

Now, assume that we are in the very special case G=P​G​L2G=PGL_{2}, TT a split torus, UU is kk-rational, 𝒢\mathcal{G} hyperspecial, rr arbitrary, and ϕ=1\phi=1 the trivial character. Compute the number of different irreducible representations appearing in RT,U,r​(1)R_{T,U,r}(1).

Solution.
As UU is kk-rational, UrU_{r} is FF-stable. It then follows that XrX_{r} is just a disjoint union of translates of UrU_{r}, indexed by (Gr/Ur)F(G_{r}/U_{r})^{F}. As UU is (the perfection of) an affine space, it only contributes to the cohomology by a degree shift. Thus, inserting ϕ=1\phi=1, we see

the induction of the trivial representation of BrFB_{r}^{F} to GrFG_{r}^{F} (it sits in one cohomological degree). The number of irreducible components of this representation is then given by the Mackey formula, which computes
(inner product on class functions of the finite group GrFG_{r}^{F}) in terms of the double cosets BrF\GrF/BrFB_{r}^{F}\backslash G_{r}^{F}/B_{r}^{F}.
